title: VRUN CTW (NES demake of Corrupt The World, NESFab, MMC3 build)
description: The MMC3 build of the VRUN NES demake (2026-10-31): the same game as vrun-nes, built with ./build.sh game --mmc3 for a TKROM-style cartridge (MMC3 / iNES mapper 4, 512 KB PRG, 128 KB CHR-ROM, 8 KB battery RAM: the Kirby's Adventure board), so it runs on carts and consoles without mapper 30 (an un-updated PowerPak, clone consoles). The mapper code is the game's swappable mapper layer (src/game/mapper_mmc3.fab beside mapper_m30.fab); docs/27-mmc3-build.md in the game repository. vrun-nes stays the mapper 30 project.

toolchain: NESFab 1.8 (ISA=legal) shipped in tools/nesfab/nesfab_legal.exe; its MMC3 far-call trampolines are patched after the build by tools/nesfab_mmc3_legal_fix.py (a NESFab bug, docs/27)

steps.name: build-game
steps.note: prebuild.sh as for vrun-nes, then prebuild_mmc3.sh (the CHR-ROM inputs); the build patches the NESFab trampolines and ends with 'PASS - ROM matches the MMC3 cartridge spec.' (tools/verify_rom_mmc3.py)

run.note: Title: NEW GAME / CONTINUE / OPTIONS. Start begins. In game, Start pauses and Select then saves (19 bytes to battery RAM at $6010).

compare.why: scripted input reached the game: the same frame number looks different with and without input

oracle.why: On the MMC3 build: Mesen 2.1.1 (the baseline the VRUN accuracy campaign used) and BrokenNes FIX cores run the same ROM with the same pad script; per frame the picture (palette indices), nametables, OAM, palette, CHR, PPU control and every APU register must agree. Uses the user's Mesen tracer, kept in BrokenDev/tools/vrun/mesen/state_trace.lua (BROKENDEV_TRACE_LUA names another).

compat.what: VRUN on other NES emulators (brokendev.ps1 compat vrun-nes-mmc3): the game's own state read through its .mlb symbols every frame, pictures at the checkpoints. Emulators boot a few frames apart, so states are compared with a frame tolerance. The map seed rotates every title frame (map_slot), so the first room may differ between emulators: current_room is recorded, never compared. The MMC3 build boots about 10 frames sooner than the mapper 30 one (no CHR upload).

scenarios.what: power-on, the title, Start, then verify's play script

checks.what: boots to the title (app_state APP_TITLE = 0 before Start)
the title runs (the NMI counter ticks)
a first boot has no save (save_exists 0)
the title looks like BrokenNes' title (structure, palette aside)
the first room finishes loading (room_load_phase reaches its last phase, 9)
the scripted play stays in the game (no death, no return to the title)
the game keeps running to the end (the NMI counter keeps ticking)
gameplay is drawn at the end

scenarios.what: Start, pause (Start), Select = save and quit: 19 bytes to the battery RAM ($6010-$6022)

checks.what: save and quit returns to the title
the title cursor lands on CONTINUE (title_cursor 1)

scenarios.what: a fresh boot of the same emulator, its battery save from 'save' in place

checks.what: a fresh boot finds the save (save_exists 1: CONTINUE is offered)
BrokenDev hardware checks (docs/projects/brokendev-debugging-plan.md, D4): every verify scenario runs again with the checks on; a finding not accepted here fails verify. Each acceptance says why.

accepted.reason: known: VRUN lags while a room loads (2 frames after Start, 5 at a room change: decompress_room, close_all_doors, spawn_hazards_from_markers); the MMC3 build has no boot-time CHR unpack (its tiles are CHR-ROM); the lagFrames budget gates normal play

budgets.what: Over a limit fails verify, near it (90%) warns; the report compares with the previous build (out/<id>/budget-history.json). romBankFree is an estimate (padding runs of 64 or more equal $00 / $FF bytes).

lagFrames.what: after the first room has loaded

busyPercent.what: the busiest frame that made it

memoryFree.what: RAM never read in the scenarios

stackFree.what: bytes between the deepest stack and the data below it

romBankFree.what: the fixed bank 31 (the code every bank calls); 2026-10-31 (MMC3 headroom work): about 1,230 bytes in runs of 32+, the largest 575 - the MMC3 layout fragments it more than mapper 30's

knownIssues: Not byte-reproducible (NESFab): compare behaviour, not file hashes.

NESFab 1.8's legal-opcode MMC3 far-call/far-jump trampolines write the even PRG bank to $8000 instead of $8001; build.sh --mmc3 patches the 6 trampolines (tools/nesfab_mmc3_legal_fix.py) until tools/nesfab is rebuilt.
An MMC3 far call costs about 36 cycles more than mapper 30's; docs/27 has the headroom numbers (sweep +2,005, boss heal +4,367 cycles on Mesen, 2026-10-31).
Do not join the music decoders into one function per track: NESFab 1.8 miscompiles it (docs/27).
NESFab miscompiles are real. When a harmless edit breaks something, disassemble before theorising.
On BrokenNes the NES runs 48.5 CPU cycles per frame more than hardware unless 'NTSC-accurate frame timing' is on. The play-ntsc scenario runs the same input with it on.
